rv.q: In this Henry Lewis-Jonathan Sayer-Henry Shields comedy where everything that can go wrong absolutely does, the result is one of the most laugh-filled works that has ever jollied a stage.
It is escapist comedy at its most outrageous, so plan your escape now to New World Stages to enjoy the Off-Broadway engagement of this irrepressible hit.
Part Monty Python, part Sherlock Holmes, this British comedy is one of New York’s funniest shows.
The pace is so relentless and the absence of anything but gags, gags, gags quickly wore out its welcome.
The bit inspires another of the several mid-play applause breaks.
Without a dull unfunny moment in this two hour production, I’d say it’s quite an achievement, one that even on second viewing, kept me laughing from the first second to the last.

cn.t: Critics hail this slapstick farce as hysterically funny with non-stop laughs from start to finish, though one dismisses it as a blatant rip-off of "Noises Off." Most agree the physical comedy and escalating chaos deliver relentless audience howls.
